symptom: The deny-only synthetic claimed-anchor and reference helpers captured a caller-controlled signature claim before their untrusted policy. A claim descriptor or ownKeys Proxy trap could repair an initially nonmatching policy anchor key digest before the policy snapshot, producing a claimedAnchorKeyDigestMatches=true for a different entry-time policy. This never established independent trust or scoring authority.
lesson: Snapshotting each input separately is insufficient when a claim Proxy is traversed before the policy it can mutate. The outer synthetic-reference helper must preserve the same policy-first ordering as claimed-anchor correlation while keeping its separate reference snapshot pinned.
guardrail: For synthetic claimed-anchor/reference deny-only correlation, pin the caller policy before traversing the caller claim, and pass that detached policy through signature math and both comparisons. Pin reference before unrelated phases. Regression tests must trigger descriptor and ownKeys claim traps, show caller policy was repaired after capture, and still deny the initially mismatching policy; keep independentAuthorityVerified=false and scoringAuthorized=false. No atomic cross-input snapshot is claimed.
